text:
incident-bot: [AUTO] Canary anomaly detected for release prompt-splitter-v2: 5xx rate spike above threshold (4.8% over 10m, baseline 0.1%). Routing to #incidents and paging on-call.
elaine: seeing a spike in customer errors on the new prompt routing path. tagging @oncall-lily and @sre-aaron — can someone take a look?
matt: digging into logs now, looks related to the experimental splitter endpoint (splitter-v2) returning empty chunks for some inputs.
oncall-lily: I'm on it. pulling canary metrics, will decide on FF kill-switch. please paste any client-visible errors here (support).
support-ryan: two paying customers reported failed completions in last 8m (acme-corp, betterinc). both were using long-context prompts and hit 5xx. ticket IDs: #4521, #4522.
sre-aaron: reproducing locally with a similar input — stacktrace points to tokenizer edge-case in the new splitter. high error rate on sequences > 8k tokens.
product-jess: what's the blast radius? is this only canary or have we pushed to more?
matt: only rolled to canary pods in us-west-2 and eu-central. rollout policy was 5% traffic. but the routing policy mistakenly sent a subset of enterprise traffic (some customers pinned) — likely why paying customers hit it.
elaine: we should flip the feature flag for prompt_splitter_v2 immediately. prepping kill-switch command.
matt: executing kill-switch now: `ffctl set prompt_splitter_v2.enabled false --actor=matt --reason="emergency 5xx on canary"`
deploy-bot: feature flag prompt_splitter_v2 set to false by matt at 1864507940. previous state: enabled=true -> enabled=false.
oncall-lily: confirming: kill-switch applied across all regions. pausing further rollout.
sre-aaron: metrics update — 5xx rate on canary down from 4.8% -> 0.3% within 60s of flag flip. latency normalizing.
incident-bot: created incident bridge: https://meet.redwood/incident/1864507890. dial-in pinned in channel.
product-jess: happy path: do we still need a rollback of image or just keep FF disabled and run a patch?
matt: rollback is low-cost for canary but code change needed for tokenizer patch. plan: leave FF off, rollback canary image to previous stable revision to ensure no accidental exposures.
deploy-bot: initiating canary rollback: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/prompt-splitter -n inference-canaries --to-revision=41`
deploy-bot: canary rollback progress: 1/3 pods updated... 2/3... 3/3. rollback successful at 1864508018.
sre-aaron: post-rollback monitoring: 5xx on canary at 0.08%, latency at baseline. customer error reports stopped.
support-ryan: notifying affected customers with an incident summary and mitigation steps. DMing legal for any escalation.
elaine: on-call handoff: @sre-aaron, I'll brief you — I'm stepping out for a quick dinner break but will remain available. Aaron, take lead for postmortem and patch timeline.
sre-aaron: taking handoff. I'll drive root cause and remediation. ETA for patch PR to fix tokenizer edge-case: 6 hours. we'll run a small canary with FF off until patch deploy.
product-jess: prepping external comms template. hold until we confirm customer list and timeline.
incident-bot: severity: Sev2. customers impacted: small subset of enterprise canary. mitigation: FF kill-switch + canary rollback.
matt: saved logs for RCA:```
ERROR prompt-splitter-v2 - tokenization failed for id=ch_9f2a: IndexError at tokenizer.py:203
stack: ...
```
oncall-lily: thanks all. final note: no full production rollout happened; alerts triggered quickly and we mitigated within ~3m from paging. I'll keep this channel open for updates until patch is in canary.
sre-aaron: short-term actions: (1) run additional validation on splitter with long-context corpora, (2) backfill tests to catch tokenization edge cases, (3) prepare hotfix PR.
elaine: please attach all relevant logs and FF audit events to the incident tracker. good catch everyone :thumbsup:
product-jess: will schedule a post-incident review tomorrow 10:30am PT.
incident-bot: incident closed to active mitigation phase at 1864508075. follow-ups assigned in tracker.
